questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code records audit events for order changes? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The database commit fails (for example a deadlock) right after record_event has run in refund_order. What is in the database?
choices: Neither the order change nor the audit row, because record_event only adds to the session and both are committed or rolled back together.
The audit row but not the order change, because audit rows use a separate transaction.
The order change but not the audit row, because the audit insert is deferred.
Both, because the audit event is flushed immediately.

questions.prompt: An admin script loads an AuditEvent through the ORM, changes its actor_id and flushes. Another script runs session.execute(update(AuditEvent).values(actor_id="x")). What happens?
choices: Both are blocked by the before_update listener.
Both succeed, because the listener only protects deletes.
The ORM edit raises RuntimeError, but the bulk update statement bypasses the mapper event and changes the rows.
The bulk update raises, but the ORM edit succeeds.

questions.prompt: An order has shipping = {"city": "Lyon", "phone": "+33 6 12 34 56 78"} and a payment_token. What do the stored before/after JSON documents contain for these fields?
choices: city, phone and payment_token in clear text, because redaction is applied only to log output.
shipping.city in clear text, while shipping.phone and payment_token are replaced by "[REDACTED]", because _redact recurses into nested dicts.
The whole shipping object replaced by "[REDACTED]".
Only payment_token redacted, because only top-level keys are checked.
